admission.justification: The leaf weighed the existing executor, an admission-only release and an unbounded queue against the removable bounded scheduler; the first two cannot reclaim queued work.

alternatives.option: A family-owned scheduler with a fixed worker count, a removable deque of pending work and one admission budget for running plus pending jobs.
alternatives.reason: It bounds physical work and lets an abandoned queued job be withdrawn before it runs.

alternatives.option: Keep ThreadPoolExecutor and release admission when a request disconnects.
alternatives.reason: Its canceled work items remain queued, so abandoned requests still grow the queue.
alternatives.reconsider_when: The executor gains a reliable remove/cancel primitive.

alternatives.option: Leave the queue unbounded and rely on worker threads only.
alternatives.reason: The round-4 finding measured retained work items at the cap; threads alone do not bound admitted work.
alternatives.reconsider_when: A measured workload shows the pending bound never binds.

consequences: The change-set route family owns 8 workers and 8 pending slots, answers 503 over the cap, returns 499 on disconnect, and reclaims abandoned queued work.
context: ThreadPoolExecutor cannot remove its canceled work items; releasing admission while leaving abandoned requests queued let the queue grow. Round 4 required a hard admission bound with reclamation.
decider: The architect's round-4 scope and the L174-A9 repair.
